note: Tone profiles for the keys lab, unapproved: each the engine sound rows it layers (`packages/engine/sounds/`), the hands each layer plays and its level, and any insert on the keys before the space (an effect of the kitchen, with its numbers). `gainDb` matches the profiles in loudness on round 1's chord-a-bar writing, near dry; it is MEASURED by the lab page (notes/rounds/liquid-keys.md). `sparseDb` (round 3) holds the match on the sparse writing, where a tone that sustains feeds a long wet tail more than one that falls: a trim per space, MEASURED as each landing's loudness over its first 3 s (BS.1770; the bare motif, 16 bars of i9 to VImaj9), against the mean of the eighteen tones in that space, averaged over the three wetness steps.

rows.name: Felt grand
rows.says: A grand with felt between hammer and string: a soft thud, round blooming chords, the top never past 2.6 kHz.

rows.name: Dark upright
rows.says: A small upright with the lid down: quick first fall, two strings beating slowly, dark and close.

rows.name: Suitcase electric piano
rows.says: A tine electric piano through its own amplifier: warm body, a faint bell at the strike, the stereo tremolo swinging the chord.

rows.name: Reed electric piano
rows.says: A reed electric piano: hollow odd harmonics with a nasal lift, a mono tremolo, a little bark when played harder.

rows.name: FM electric piano
rows.says: The two-operator electric piano played softly: a clean pitched body, the brightness only in the first half second.

rows.name: Glassy electric piano
rows.says: A pure electric piano body under a high glassy tine that rings a moment: clear, wide and long.

rows.name: Electric piano and haze
rows.says: The soft FM electric piano with a dark wavetable haze swelling under the right hand, nine decibels back.

rows.name: Lo-fi tape piano
rows.says: A worn small piano through a tired tape head: the top rolled off at 3 kHz, the pitch wandering slowly.

rows.name: Vibes and electric piano
rows.says: The suitcase electric piano doubled in the right hand by a soft-mallet vibraphone, its discs pulsing slowly.

rows.name: Mellow bright grand
rows.says: A clearer grand: six stretched partials, a soft tick of hammer and a gentle lid at 3.6 kHz, present without glare.

rows.name: Close soft grand
rows.says: An intimate grand heard from just over the strings, played soft: the felt landing, the chord in tune and full, a warm low end.

swap.says: where a bird's swap sounds this tone over the one the draw chose (PLAN-UNIFY U3) and the drawn tone's inserts cannot pay for its EQ: the note's own low-pass at 0.95, matched by measure (seed 1 at the Drum & Bass tile, Zephyr 0.2, 196-232 s, the keys alone: over 1.5 kHz at the onsets -21.2 dB with the EQ and at 0.95, the attack over 2 kHz -39.0 and -38.9; the EQ's low shelf has no stand-in)

rows.name: Muted felt upright
rows.says: An upright with the practice felt down: a soft thud, the top gone at once, short dark notes with a honky warmth.

rows.name: Warm grand, far back
rows.says: A big warm concert grand heard from the back of the hall: the air takes its top, the room's early reflections soften its strike, a long tail.

swap.says: where a bird's swap sounds this tone over the one the draw chose (PLAN-UNIFY U3), at no more cost: its room (a 1.2 s reverb at 0.4 mix) a send to the field's shared hall with the note's direct at the room's dry share, 0.6, the send matched on the room's body by measure (seed 1 at the Drum & Bass tile, Zephyr 0.2, a lone chord at 88 s, the keys alone: the room 17.7 dB under the dry body, the hall at 0.12 17.3; its first 300 ms 11.7 against 17.2 and its tail after 0.5 s 42 against 57, both 15 dB or more under the grand's own decay, so the whole keys' level and tails land within 0.4 dB of the grand with its own room); its EQ the note's own low-pass at 0.8 where the drawn tone's inserts cannot pay for it (the EQ cuts above 3 kHz, where this grand has nothing: 84 dB under; its centroid 399 Hz with its own EQ and room, 372 swapped)

rows.name: Cassette upright
rows.says: A home upright on a worn cassette: the top gone at 2.3 kHz, the tape's wow pulling the pitch well off and back, a little saturation.

rows.name: Electric grand
rows.says: An electric grand with a slow chorus: stiff short strings through a pickup, a zing at the strike, a quick plucky fall.

rows.name: Dark tine electric piano
rows.says: An older, darker tine electric piano: a woody body, a soft bark when the chord is struck and no tremolo, through a warm amplifier.

swap.says: where a bird's swap sounds this tone over the one the draw chose (PLAN-UNIFY U3) and the drawn tone's inserts cannot pay for its drive: the note's own low-pass at 0.35, matched by measure on the energy over 1.5 kHz at the onsets (seed 1 at the Drum & Bass tile, Zephyr 0.2, 196-232 s, the keys alone: -29.5 dB with the drive, -29.6 at 0.35; the 1-3 kHz band 3.6 dB under the drive's, its attack over 2 kHz 3.8 dB over it: a filter is not a drive)

rows.name: Reed piano, small amp
rows.says: A mellow reed electric piano through a small amplifier: hollow and boxy, the lows and the top left out by the little speaker, a slow tremolo.

rows.name: Felt grand and sine
rows.says: The felt grand doubled by a quiet near-pure sine: the strike is the piano's, and the sine holds the chord round once the strings fall.
